cards.explanation: The answer is four great beasts, friends. The winds churn the sea and up they come, and Daniel says each one is different from the others. I like a surprise, but four of them out of one sea is a lot of surprises. I'd be checking the water before I got anywhere near it.

The answer is False. Daniel says the beasts came up out of the sea, “…each one different from the others…” A lion-like one, a bear-like one, a leopard-like one, and a fourth unlike all the rest are coming. Nobody's confusing these four in a lineup.

The answer is that the wings are torn off. Daniel says, “I watched until its wings were torn off…” The beast starts out looking ready to fly and ends up on its feet. After that it's lifted up from the ground and made to stand on two feet like a man.

The answer is man. The beast is made to stand on two feet like a man and given the mind of a man. The wings come off, and the beast goes through a big change. Hang onto that one, friends, because this vision has plenty of changes.

The answer is that it's told to get up and gorge on flesh. The beast is told, “Get up and gorge yourself on flesh!” Three ribs between its teeth, and it still gets orders for more. The text says it was told, and it doesn't say who by, so I'll leave that open too.

The answer is True. Daniel says of the leopard-like beast, “…it was given authority to rule.” It gets four wings and four heads and authority on top of that. The text says it was given authority, and it doesn't say by whom.

The answer is that it tramples it underfoot. Daniel says the fourth beast “…devoured and crushed; then it trampled underfoot whatever was left.” First the teeth, then the feet. I don't think anything gets left over after that.

The answer is that they're uprooted before it. Daniel says three of the first horns “…were uprooted before it.” The little horn comes up and three of the ten are gone. For a little horn, that's a big effect.
The answer is arrogance. The horn has eyes like those of a man and a mouth that spoke words of arrogance. Daniel looks at it closely, and it's talking big. I'd keep an eye on that mouth too, friends.

The answer is True. Daniel says, “A river of fire was flowing, coming out from His presence.” The throne is already flaming with fire, with its wheels ablaze. So the whole scene is lit up around the Ancient of Days.

The answer is thousands upon thousands. Daniel says, “Thousands upon thousands attended Him, and myriads upon myriads stood before Him.” That's a crowd far past counting. Imagine me trying to bake for that many.

The answer is that the beast is slain and thrown into the fire. Daniel says, “…the beast was slain, and its body was destroyed and thrown into the blazing fire.” He kept watching because of the arrogant words, and this is what he saw. The loud horn doesn't get the last word.

The answer is True. Daniel says, “As for the rest of the beasts, their dominion was removed, but they were granted an extension of life for a season and a time.” Their rule is taken away, and their lives go on for a while. The text doesn't say more than that, so neither will I.
The answer is serve. He's given dominion, glory and kingship. Daniel says it's “…that the people of every nation and language should serve Him.” That's every nation and every language, friends.

The answer is a kingdom that will never be destroyed. Daniel says, “…His kingdom is one that will never be destroyed.” His dominion is everlasting and will not pass away. Compare that with the rest of the beasts, whose dominion was removed (Daniel 7:12).

The answer is that he asks someone standing there what it means. Daniel says, “I approached one of those who were standing there, and I asked him the true meaning of all this.” He doesn't sit with his alarm. He goes and asks someone, and I think that's wise.

The answer is False. The explainer says the four beasts are four kings who will arise from the earth. Then he says, “But the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever…” It's the saints who receive it.

The answer is forever and ever, friends. The explainer says the saints “…will receive the kingdom and possess it forever…” and then he adds, yes, forever and ever. He says it twice. That's the kind of repeating I can get behind.

The answer is the saints of the Most High. Daniel says, “…this horn was waging war against the saints and prevailing against them…” This is a heavy part of the vision. The Most High is God, and these are His people.

The answer is True, and I think it's a hard line to read. Daniel says the horn was “…waging war against the saints and prevailing against them…” But keep going, friends, because the verse after that has a turn. It's the turn that matters.

The answer is the Ancient of Days. Daniel says He “…arrived and pronounced judgment in favor of the saints of the Most High…” Then the time came for them to possess the kingdom. That's the UNTIL, and He's the one in it.

The answer is ten kings who rise from it. The explainer says, “…the ten horns are ten kings who will rise from this kingdom.” So the horns on the beast's head stand for kings. They come out of the fourth kingdom.
The answer is False. The explainer says another king will rise after the ten, “…different from the earlier ones…” He will also subdue three kings. This one doesn't match the rest.

The answer is a time and times and half a time. The explainer says the saints “…will be given into his hand for a time, and times, and half a time.” It's a heavy stretch, and the text gives it in exactly those words. I won't try to turn it into a number.

The answer is that it's taken away and destroyed forever. The explainer says, “But the court will convene, and his dominion will be taken away and completely destroyed forever.” The court sits, and the horn's rule is gone. The big talker doesn't come out ahead.
The answer is pale. Daniel says, “…my thoughts troubled me greatly, and my face turned pale.” That's the face of a man who just saw all that. I'd probably need to sit down too, friends.
The answer is that he keeps it to himself. Daniel says, “But I kept the matter to myself.” The text doesn't tell us why, so I won't guess. It leaves it at that.
